place.id: Selat Karimata dan Laut Jawa bagian utara (kotak indeks CENS: 105–115°BT, 5°LS–ekuator)
place.en: Karimata Strait and the northern Java Sea (CENS index box: 105–115°E, 5°S–equator)

summary.id: Aliran angin utara di lapisan bawah atmosfer yang sesekali menembus khatulistiwa dari Laut Cina Selatan ke Laut Jawa pada musim dingin belahan bumi utara, dan berkaitan dengan hujan lebat di Jawa dan sekitarnya.
summary.en: A low-level northerly flow that intermittently pushes across the equator from the South China Sea into the Java Sea in northern-hemisphere winter, linked to heavy rain over Java and nearby areas.

scientific.id: Cross Equatorial Northerly Surge (CENS) adalah aliran angin utara di lapisan bawah atmosfer yang sesekali menembus khatulistiwa di atas Laut Cina Selatan bagian selatan dan Benua Maritim, terutama antara Oktober dan April. Hattori, Mori, dan Matsumoto (2011) mendefinisikan satu kejadian CENS sebagai periode ketika rata-rata angin utara di kotak 105–115°BT dan 5°LS sampai ekuator, dihitung dari angin permukaan laut satelit QuikSCAT, terus melebihi 5 m/s; hari dengan indeks tertinggi dijadikan hari 0. Dalam 10 musim dingin (Desember 2000 sampai Maret 2009) mereka menemukan 62 kejadian: 11 berkaitan dengan lonjakan udara dingin dari daratan Asia (cold surge), 20 dengan variasi intramusiman tropis seperti MJO, 16 dengan keduanya, dan 15 dengan keduanya tidak. Rata-rata lama indeks di atas 5 m/s sekitar 6 hari pada pola lonjakan dingin, 4 hari pada pola MJO, dan 5 hari pada pola gabungan. Menurut studi itu, kemunculan CENS merupakan faktor lingkungan penting bagi hujan di atas rata-rata yang luas di Benua Maritim: hujan bertambah terutama di utara Pulau Jawa pada pola lonjakan dingin, di barat Sumatra dan selatan Jawa pada pola MJO, dan paling besar pada pola gabungan, termasuk di Jawa barat laut. Manual satelit EUMeTrain menggambarkan kasus banjir Jakarta awal 2007: lonjakan dimulai sekitar 26 Januari 2007, melintasi ekuator dengan angin utara lebih dari 5 m/s pada 29 Januari, dan hujan terlebat di Jawa Barat terjadi pada 1–2 Februari; stasiun Kemayoran mencatat 234 mm pada 1 Februari, dibandingkan dengan rata-rata bulanan Jakarta sekitar 300 mm. Manual itu juga mencatat bahwa pusaran Borneo muncul pada sekitar 60 % kasus lonjakan dingin dan membatasi laju lonjakan ke selatan.
scientific.en: The cross-equatorial northerly surge (CENS) is a low-level northerly flow that intermittently crosses the equator over the southern South China Sea and the Maritime Continent, mainly between October and April. Hattori, Mori and Matsumoto (2011) defined one CENS event as a period when the area-averaged northerly wind over 105–115°E and 5°S to the equator, computed from QuikSCAT satellite sea-surface wind, stays above 5 m/s; the day of the highest index is taken as day 0. In 10 winters (December 2000 to March 2009) they found 62 events: 11 tied to cold surges from the Asian continent, 20 to tropical intraseasonal variations such as the MJO, 16 to both, and 15 to neither. The index stayed above 5 m/s for about 6 days on average in the cold-surge pattern, 4 days in the MJO pattern and 5 days in the combined pattern. According to that study, CENS is an important environmental factor for widespread above-normal rain over the Maritime Continent: rain increases mainly north of Java in the cold-surge pattern, west of Sumatra and south of Java in the MJO pattern, and most in the combined pattern, including north-western Java. The EUMeTrain satellite manual describes the early-2007 Jakarta flood case: the surge started around 26 January 2007, crossed the equator with northerly winds above 5 m/s on 29 January, and the heaviest rain in West Java fell on 1–2 February; Kemayoran station recorded 234 mm on 1 February, against a Jakarta monthly average of about 300 mm. The manual also notes a Borneo vortex in about 60 % of cold-surge cases, which limits how far south the surge advances.

caveat.id: Indeks pada grafik adalah perkiraan kami sendiri dari angin 925 hPa reanalisis NCEP/NCAR (rata-rata harian, kisi 2,5°), bukan indeks asli Hattori dkk. (2011) yang dihitung dari angin permukaan laut QuikSCAT. Angkanya tidak sama: pada Desember 2006–Maret 2007 perkiraan ini hanya mencapai 5 m/s pada 3 hari (27 Desember, 2 dan 3 Februari), jadi garis 5 m/s hanyalah acuan ambang mereka, bukan penentu kejadian di sini. Studi Hattori memakai data 2000–2009; kasus 2007 dan angka hujannya berasal dari manual EUMeTrain, bukan dari studi Hattori. Peta menunjukkan kondisi atmosfer pada hari-hari itu; kisi 2,5° terlalu kasar untuk detail lonjakan.
caveat.en: The index on the chart is our own estimate from 925 hPa NCEP/NCAR reanalysis wind (daily means, 2.5° grid), not the original index of Hattori et al. (2011), which was computed from QuikSCAT sea-surface wind. The values differ: over December 2006–March 2007 this estimate reaches 5 m/s on only 3 days (27 December, 2 and 3 February), so the 5 m/s line is only their threshold for reference, not what decides an event here. Hattori's study used 2000–2009 data; the 2007 case and its rainfall figures come from the EUMeTrain manual, not from Hattori's study. The maps show the state of the atmosphere on those days; a 2.5° grid is too coarse for the finer detail of a surge.

sources.text: Hattori, M., Mori, S. and Matsumoto, J. (2011), “The Cross-Equatorial Northerly Surge over the Maritime Continent and Its Relationship to Precipitation Patterns”, Journal of the Meteorological Society of Japan 89A, 27–47 (open access)

curator_notes: Hattori et al. (2011): I read the full text myself (open-access PDF, pdftotext) up to the start of the precipitation section; the abstract and methods are checked, the precipitation section only through its abstract-level statements. Details to check against the PDF: definition (QuikSCAT, 105-115E, 5S-EQ, > 5 m/s continuously = one event; day 0 = maximum; events within 3 days of a former one excluded from composites), 62 events (11/20/16/15), mean duration above 5 m/s about 6/4/5 days (CS/MJO/CS-MJO), precipitation locations from the abstract.

EUMeTrain (Northerly Cold Surge manual): read through a fetch agent's account (it says full text), not verbatim. Facts used: the 26 Jan start, 28 Jan NE wind > 8 m/s over the SCS, 29 Jan equator crossing with northerlies > 5 m/s, heaviest rain 1-2 Feb in West Java, Kemayoran 234 mm on 1 Feb vs about 300 mm monthly average, Borneo vortex in about 60 % of cold-surge cases (same figure as the Borneo vortex entry). Please skim the page. It also lists other indices (cold surge index 925 hPa > 8 m/s at 15N 110-117.5E) not used here.

The map and the index are my own plots/estimates from NCEP/NCAR Reanalysis 1 (925 hPa wind and sea-level pressure, daily means, 2.5 degree grid; the index is the mean of 15 grid points in the Hattori box, northerly positive). They are NOT the QuikSCAT index: the series peaks at 5.4 m/s on 2-3 Feb 2007, the highest of December 2006-March 2007, and passes 5 m/s on only 3 days. The page says all of this.

Case choice: 25 Jan - 9 Feb 2007 is the Jakarta flood case that EUMeTrain walks through, and Hattori's introduction cites Wu et al. (2007) on the same 2007 event (strongest northerly event crossed the equator, persisted over a week, repeated torrential rain). I did NOT read Wu et al. (2007) or the Kyoto MWR paper (MWR-D-11-00094; the repository returned an empty page); both would be good extra sources for the 2007 case. The Borneo Vortex entry uses the same week, with its own caveat.

Not found / not used: BMKG's own CENS explainer or index (the search found papers citing Hattori but no BMKG page); other papers that use 850 or 925 hPa indices with different thresholds (they exist: indices vary by study). A BMKG page would help the Indonesian text.
Name: no Indonesian or local name is listed; name_id keeps the English-derived acronym used by BMKG-affiliated papers. Pin (-2.5, 110.0) is the centre of the index box, not a place where it 'occurs'.
documentation: 'well' is my choice (a defining paper plus a satellite manual and a well-known 2007 case). Photo: none. Local knowledge: none (needs a named source).
